findings.passage: While two years old already, the legislature also approved legislation that requires individuals to present photo identification when they vote. Acceptable forms of identification include a Kentucky driver’s license or any military, college and Kentucky government IDs. While opponents of this measure claimed it might prevent some Kentuckians from voting, we made it easier to get an ID card since voters can get a free, state-issued ID card if they are at least 18 years old
findings.note: Column signed by the member, published on K105 (her own column, not a reporter's words). Describes the photo-ID-to-vote law, lists accepted IDs, and says a free state ID is available.

findings.passage: The names of more than 166,000 individuals ineligible to vote, including 136,000 deceased voters were purged from the system over the past several years. Others no longer live in Kentucky or are otherwise ineligible.
findings.note: Same column. Describes voter-roll cleanup as part of the state's election security steps.
